explanations.answer: One on the sea and one on the land
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The angel "placed his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land." (Revelation 10:2) One foot in the water, one foot on the ground, and a little scroll lying open in his hand. I can barely keep both feet on my gold base when the floor gets sticky.

explanations.answer: One on the mountain and one in the valley
explanations.explanation: Close on the size of it, friend, because this angel is big. But the text doesn't mention a mountain or a valley. It says he placed his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land (Revelation 10:2). That's a wide stance, and I think my back would file a complaint.

explanations.answer: One on the river and one on the shore
explanations.explanation: A river and a shore would be a nice spot to stand, baker. But John says the angel placed his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land (Revelation 10:2). The sea is a lot more water than a river. And he's holding a small scroll lying open the whole time.

Oh, I see why you went there, friend. John says he was about to put it in writing. But then a voice from heaven said, “Seal up what the seven thunders have said, and do not write it down.” (Revelation 10:4) So the pen never touched the page for that one.

That's right, baker. John was about to write it down, and then the voice from heaven stopped him. It said, “Seal up what the seven thunders have said, and do not write it down.” (Revelation 10:4) So John kept it sealed. I can't even keep a cookie recipe to myself, and he kept thunder.

I get the mix-up, friend, because the thunders just spoke in the verses before. But the angel doesn't swear by them. He swears by “Him who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and everything in it, the earth and everything in it, and the sea and everything in it.” (Revelation 10:6) That's the Creator, and nobody else.

Right, baker. The angel lifts his right hand to heaven and swears by “Him who lives forever and ever.” (Revelation 10:6) That's the One who created heaven, the earth and the sea, and everything in them. The thunders spoke earlier, but he doesn't swear by them.

explanations.answer: There will be no more delay
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. The angel says, “There will be no more delay!” (Revelation 10:6) He swears it by the One who created everything, so he's saying it with his hand raised. I wish my oven timer sounded that sure of itself.

Good guess, friend, since the thunders were just in the scene. But the thunders' words were sealed, and the angel doesn't say they'll speak again. What he swears is, “There will be no more delay!” (Revelation 10:6) That's the whole announcement.

Careful, baker. The scroll in the angel's hand is the one that "lay open." (Revelation 10:2) The thing that was sealed up was what the seven thunders said (Revelation 10:4). The angel's announcement is, “There will be no more delay!” (Revelation 10:6)

Yes, baker. The angel says that when the seventh angel begins to sound his trumpet, “the mystery of God will be fulfilled.” (Revelation 10:7) I'm not going to guess past that, because the text doesn't. I just keep my ovens ready.

That phrase does show up in Revelation, friend, but it's not what the angel says here. He says that in the days of the seventh angel, “the mystery of God will be fulfilled.” (Revelation 10:7) That's the thing getting fulfilled in this verse.

Good try, baker, because Revelation does talk about harvests elsewhere. But this angel says something different. When the seventh angel begins to sound his trumpet, “the mystery of God will be fulfilled.” (Revelation 10:7) I'd stick to what he actually says, like I stick to the recipe.

That's right, baker. The mystery of God will be fulfilled “just as He proclaimed to His servants the prophets.” (Revelation 10:7) So God said it first, and the angel says it's coming. That's a pretty good track record.

Kings do show up at the end of this passage, friend. John is told to prophesy about them (Revelation 10:11). But the angel says God proclaimed this to “His servants the prophets.” (Revelation 10:7) Different group, baker.

The elders are in Revelation, baker, but not in this verse. The angel says it will be fulfilled “just as He proclaimed to His servants the prophets.” (Revelation 10:7) The prophets are the ones who got the word.

explanations.answer: Take the small scroll from the angel
explanations.explanation: You've got it, baker. The voice says, “Go, take the small scroll that lies open in the hand of the angel standing on the sea and on the land.” (Revelation 10:8) That's a big angel to walk up to. I'd be asking if there's a side door.

explanations.answer: Write a letter to the seven churches
explanations.explanation: That job does belong to John, friend, but it's from the beginning of the book (Revelation 1:11). Here the voice from heaven says, “Go, take the small scroll that lies open in the hand of the angel standing on the sea and on the land.” (Revelation 10:8) Different job, same John.

explanations.answer: Count the servants who were sealed
explanations.explanation: Sealed servants do show up in Revelation, baker. But nobody asks John to count them here. The voice tells him, “Go, take the small scroll that lies open in the hand of the angel standing on the sea and on the land.” (Revelation 10:8)

Yes, baker. The angel says, “It will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be as sweet as honey.” (Revelation 10:9) Sweet going down and bitter after. I've had a cookie like that once, and I blame the raisins.

You'd think a whole scroll would fill a person up, friend. But the angel says, “It will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be as sweet as honey.” (Revelation 10:9) He says bitter, not full.

Warm sounds cozy, baker, like a fresh batch. But the angel doesn't say that. He says, “It will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be as sweet as honey.” (Revelation 10:9) The word he uses is bitter.

That's right, baker. John says he ate it, “and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth. But when I had eaten it, my stomach turned bitter.” (Revelation 10:10) Same two things the angel told him, in the same order. Nothing came out different.

I see why you'd doubt it, friend, but it matches. The angel said it would be sweet as honey in his mouth and make his stomach bitter (Revelation 10:9). John says, “it was as sweet as honey in my mouth. But when I had eaten it, my stomach turned bitter.” (Revelation 10:10) The angel called it, start to finish.

explanations.answer: Prophesy again about many peoples and kings
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. John is told, “You must prophesy again about many peoples and nations and tongues and kings.” (Revelation 10:11) So the scroll isn't the end of his job. It's more like the start of the next part.

explanations.answer: Wait in silence for the last trumpet
explanations.explanation: Waiting is a real thing, friend, and I know plenty about it. But John isn't told to be silent. He's told, “You must prophesy again about many peoples and nations and tongues and kings.” (Revelation 10:11) That sounds like a lot of talking to me.

explanations.answer: Keep the vision sealed for a while
explanations.explanation: Something was sealed earlier, baker, but it was what the seven thunders said (Revelation 10:4). This time John is told, “You must prophesy again about many peoples and nations and tongues and kings.” (Revelation 10:11) That's the opposite of keeping quiet.
